http://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/25/.text: World / Europe Romania shoots down second drone in two days Published: 25 Jul 2026 - 10:25 am | Last Updated: 25 Jul 2026 - 10:27 am Representational image AFP Bucharest: Romania shot down a drone in its airspace on Saturday for the second day in a row, marking the second time since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, it said. The NATO member bordering Ukraine has seen frequent drone incursions, including drones crashing on its soil, since 2022. Its forces shot down a drone for the first time on Friday, around 114 kilometres (70 miles) from Bucharest. The military took down another drone, which "had illegally entered Romanian airspace", on Saturday at 8:34am (0534 GMT), according to defence minister Radu Miruta. It was shot down 9.6 kilometres (six miles) west of Sfantu Gheorghe in the Danube Delta near the border with Ukraine, he added. "The drone was detected by Ministry of National Defence radars entering our airspace at 8:22 and was struck a few minutes later by a Romanian F-16 fighter jet," he posted on Facebook. Drone incursions in Romania have been detected dozens of times since the start of the Ukraine war. A drone smashed into an apartment building in May, wounding two people and drawing condemnation from NATO and the European Union, which blamed Russia and warned against further incursions. https://www.politico.eu/article/eu-chief.text: Kaja Kallas, the EU's chief diplomat, announced Tuesday a high-level group made of former political and military leaders who will reflect on how the bloc can defend itself amid a changing U.S. presence. The new body, which will be launched next week, will include prominent figures from the European Union as well as the United Kingdom and Ukraine, she announced at the start of an informal defense ministers' meeting in Ireland. "Of course NATO remains the cornerstone of our European security. At the same time, the United States is also calling on European allies to assume greater responsibility for our own defense," said Kallas, who coordinates foreign and security policy on behalf of the EU's 27 member countries. "Why have these political and military leaders? They can also say things that we, as institutions, cannot," she added. A spokesperson for Kallas did not specify who will join the group. The former Estonian prime minister added that the aim of the group was not to work on replicating U.S. defense capabilities but to focus on defending European territory by using "unique strengths" while also using the "extensive operational experience of Ukraine" to "challenge conventional thinking." https://www.dw.com/en/iran-denies-role-i.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5PIII Prefer DW on Google The apparent cyberattack forced hundreds of supermarkets to throw out spoiled produce after the refrigeration and freezer units went into a high-temperature defrost cycle Image: Elsa Rancel/Ouest-France/PHOTOPQR/MAXPPP/IMAGO Advertisement Iran on Tuesday dismissed French accusations that its Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) was behind a cyberattack on hundreds of supermarkets last month , as Paris summoned Tehran's ambassador to discuss the incident. "Iran's Foreign Ministry categorically rejects the French government's baseless and one-sided accusations against Iran regarding alleged cyber activities in France ," the ministry said, adding that it "strongly condemns this hackneyed policy of leveling accusations against the Islamic Republic." The alleged attack, which began overnight on October 11-12, raised the temperatures in supermarket refrigerators and freezer units , spoiling produce and even causing fires in isolated instances. A series of similar incidents have since followed in Europe and beyond , even including a failed attack on cooling units at French blood banks this month , though it is not yet clear if these subsequent events are connected. France summons ambassador, says it rules 'nothing' out in response French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said on Tuesday that his government would "rule nothing out and will take all measures — including those we may not disclose publicly — that we deem proportionate and necessary to deter any further attacks." Barrot was speaking amid a G7 foreign ministers' meeting in Paris that included discussions with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on the conflict with Iran . Barrot even said that despite a change in tone from the Trump administration since the midterm election defeat in the US , the risk of a renewed escalation with Iran could not be ruled out, "otherwise, we would not have devoted so much time and energy over the past two days to addressing these issues with our American counterpart." Barrot hosted G7 foreign ministers, including US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, in Paris this week Image: Brendan Smialowski/REUTERS France summoned the Iranian ambassador on Tuesday and said it would be seeking European-level sanctions in response. The EU said it would seek to provide a "swift and united response" pending discussion with member states. "As the EU, we have consistently called on all states to refrain from malicious behavior in the cyberspace, and we will continue to address such malicious behavior, making use of all the tools that we have, also under the EU cyber diplomacy toolbox, including sanctions," spokesman Anouar El Anouni said. Barrot said that the goal of any response would be "to deter anyone who might be tempted, in Iran or elsewhere, to do it again." Iran accuses French of 'projecting' its own failures Tehran appeared to threaten retaliatory measures of its own if sanctions materialized, saying it would "not hesitate to take necessary and appropriate measures to safeguard its national interests and security in the face of unlawful foreign activities." It accused France of "merely projecting its own governance failures" with its allegations. "A government that cannot even manage the temperature of its own refrigerators now seeks to shift the blame onto foreign actors through these preposterous accusations," it said. Around 700 supermarkets, of a total of roughly 10,000 across France, were affected by the alleged cyberattack Image: Stephane Mahe/REUTERS What did Paris prosecutors say about suspected Iranian involvement? Paris prosecutor Laure Beccuau said on Monday that she had opened an investigation into leading members of Shahid Kaveh, a cyber unit that is part of Iran's multi-force specialist military, the IRGC, that answers directly to its religious leadership. She said her office had requested arrest warrants against two Shahid Kaveh officials and was investigating others. She described the entity as "an offensive cyber unit affiliated with the Electronic and Cyber Center of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps." French cyber intelligence agencies said the unit conducted "large-scale campaigns targeting industrial equipment for the purpose of sabotage." It said it primarily targeted Israel and the US, but also France and other European countries. Beccuau said that the attack targeted roughly 700 of France's roughly 10,000 supermarkets. It used web interfaces to "initiate abnormal, indefinite defrost cycles," and also to disable automated alerts from sensors designed to go off when temperatures exceeded certain levels. Sweden's Civil Defense Minister Carl-Oskar Bohlin warned that more cyberattacks could be expected in the coming months, as AI tools make it easier to detect and exploit vulnerabilities. He said that it was not yet possible to say if hacks targeted Swedish supermarkets last week were connected, not least because the type of sabotage would have "been easy to copy" after seeing the initial reports in October. https://www.dw.com/en/microsoft-works-to.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5POu3 Prefer DW on Google Beyond Microsoft's e-mail program Outlook being down, Teams and Copilot were also hit in Thursday's outage Image: Sk Mijanur Rahaman/imageBROKER/picture alliance Advertisement Software giant Microsoft on Thursday said it was working to fix a global outage affecting its Microsoft 365 apps, including Outlook and Teams. Outage tracker Downdetector received reports from 74 countries and territories within about an hour. The outage, which blocked users from accessing their e-mail and other services, also impacted Microsoft 365 connectors used by the companies OpenAI and Anthropic , which said tools were not working as expected. Downdetector logged nearly 130,000 US reports of Outlook problems shortly after 1 p.m. EST (1800 GMT). Some customers reported having trouble sending and receiving e-mail; others said the program was entirely inaccessible. Outages of the Teams workplace messaging app were also reported, as well as other Microsoft 365 services such as the AI assistant Copilot. Microsoft initially said on X that it was aware that users were "experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas," noting that part of its infrastructure was "experiencing elevated load" that was "likely contributing to connectivity errors." "We are aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact," it added. Microsoft said some restarted servers stopped responding again once traffic returned. In an update at 0254 GMT Friday, the company said its latest changes had not worked as expected and that it was looking for other ways to restore service. Can you survive without US tech?
